name: 43586-tiledimage-dsocr3b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine (`--distributed-executor-backend uni`), no worker processes.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams = 8, warmup the first 20%, bounded at 1000 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: Single-turn document OCR, one image per request: guidellm `synthetic_text` (16 prompt tokens, min = max) composed with one `synthetic_image` source (1024x1024 JPEG, quality 85, `noise` content, `images_per_request: 1`, seed 43586), 8 output tokens with EOS ignored, `request_format: plain`, greedy. Every image is distinct, so no request is served out of a cache hit.
purpose: A document OCR service reading single page images into short text replies, eight concurrent users, one GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: vLLM at commit b2cfae777dbad80096e5969212da58ff01cc432e. The interpreter that runs it
# and the hardware seal live in configs/env.yaml, which is not portable.

model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR

# Required, not boilerplate: the checkpoint ships its own config and processor classes
# (`auto_map`) and will not load without it.
trust-remote-code: true

dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 8192

# Not the engine default at this commit (2048). Declared, not redundant -- do not drop it.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# Must match scenario.json's single image source: it is both the admission limit and what the
# engine's startup profiling pass is sized against. Change one and you must change the other.
limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 1, "video": 0}

enable-prefix-caching: false
mm-processor-cache-gb: 0
distributed-executor-backend: uni
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# MACHINE WORKAROUND, applied to every run.
# NOT a tuning knob: the KV pool is nowhere near binding here and this value cannot change what
# is measured. The load is eight streams of ~718 tokens = ~5.7k resident tokens; at 12 layers x
# 10 KV heads x 128 x 2 x bf16 = 60 KiB/token, that is 0.34 GiB against a pool still >20 GiB at
# the value below. What the engine default (0.92) does instead is demand 72.85 of the card's
# 79.19 GiB be FREE at start-up and then leave no headroom for the rest of start-up profiling,
# which on this shared partition fails the run outright in two different ways.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.55

# MACHINE WORKAROUND, applied to every run.
# On this H100 / driver-570 partition the engine's default choice for this checkpoint aborts the
# process with SIGFPE during start-up profiling, before a single request is served, and leaves no
# Python traceback anywhere. Pinning the version below is what makes the engine reach the serving
# loop at all. It is not a tuning knob: drop it and the run reports rc=0 with zero successful
# requests.
attention-config: {"flash_attn_version": 2}
